subject: EU/APAC private deploy: node affinity + evacuation guide and decision request
messages:
From: John Li <john.li@acme-fin.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: acme-cloud-ops@acme-fin.com
Date: 2026-07-18T07:12:00Z
Subject: Private deployment cutover: EU->APAC node affinity and evacuation planning

Evelyn —

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. As Acme prepares its phased private deployment across EU and APAC clusters, we need a short decision from Redwood on how node affinity and evacuation should be handled to satisfy our EU data residency controls and APAC DR requirements.

High level asks:
- For EU-origin traffic, must remain pinned to EU nodes unless an authorized cross-border exception is triggered.
- For failover, we need an ordered eviction/evacuation plan that preserves custody evidence (KMS provenance + audit logs) and a clear authorization chain.
- We also need recommended retention/time-to-live on cached KV/prefix data during cross-region evacs.

I attached a simple zone map and our regulatory note. Can your team propose the minimal set of controls we should enforce on the VPC/private control plane so our auditors are satisfied?

Thanks —
John Li
Head of Cloud Ops, Acme Financial Services
[Attachment: acme-zone-map-v2.pdf (PDF)]

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: John Li <john.li@acme-fin.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-18T12:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Private deployment cutover: EU->APAC node affinity and evacuation planning

John —

Appreciate the clear asks. Quick confirmation: we can provide a prescriptive playbook that covers node affinity, explicit cross-border exception workflow (with owner, approval TTL, and audit evidence), and KV/cache retention behavior during evacuation.

I’ll pull in Karthik (networking) and Soojin (privacy/compliance) to scope the constraints and give a recommended config you can bake into your acceptance criteria.

Two quick clarifications before we draft the playbook:
1) Does Acme require that KMS keys remain in-region (yes/no) for the EU tenant when failed-over to APAC, or is wrapping with a Redwood-managed key acceptable for the failover window?
2) For warm standby activation, what RPO (max lag in seconds) do you need for in-memory caches vs persisted stores?

If you can reply to those two items we’ll aim to send a short playbook by EOD tomorrow.

—Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: proposed-evacuation-playbook.md (draft)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-19T09:18:00Z
Subject: RE: Private deployment cutover: EU->APAC node affinity and evacuation planning

Folks —

Sketched the technical constraints and suggested defaults below (keeping auditor appetite and minimal operational blast radius in mind):

1) Node affinity model (recommended):
   - Tenant-level routing: tag tenant metadata with data_residency = {EU, APAC}. All requests from EU logical tenants route to EU-private-cluster nodes by default.
   - Cross-border exception: a signed, timebound token (signed by customer SSO and Redwood operator) allows routing to APAC nodes for a set TTL (default 4 hours). Token issuance events are logged to the audit stream.

2) KMS & keys:
   - Strong preferred mode: customer-managed KMS with regional key (EU) only. On failover, do NOT import or export key material to APAC.
   - Fallback: if Acme cannot meet KMS geo-restriction, Redwood can use a transient-wrapping key (customer encrypted) that preserves envelope provenance. This must be explicitly authorized and recorded.

3) Evacuation sequencing and custody evidence:
   - Evac step 1 (read-only freeze): mark EU nodes as read-only for affected tenant and flush KV prefix writes to durable store before evacuation.
   - Evac step 2 (KV snapshot): create a signed snapshot manifest with hash + KMS envelope metadata; copy manifest to a regional evidence bucket (EU-only).
   - Evac step 3 (failover proxy): issue cross-border token (if authorized) and shift traffic to APAC nodes. All traffic routed to APAC must carry original request context and the snapshot manifest id.
   - Audit logging: every step emits an immutable event to the audit stream (timestamped, signed).

4) Cache retention defaults:
   - In-memory prefix/KV: TTL = min(15 minutes, RPO/4). Default suggested RPO for warm-standby = 2 minutes (so default cache TTL ~30s).
   - Durable persisted store: preserve all writes; snapshots stored with KMS metadata and retention per Acme policy.

5) Operational guardrails:
   - Auto-evac disabled by default; evacuations require a two-person approval (customer + Redwood ops) unless emergency escalation is invoked.
   - Canary routing: if cross-border exception smaller than 1% traffic for 10 minutes, auto-revert.

I’ll draft a short playbook with exact command sequences we would run from the Redwood private control plane. Jordan — can you add the CLI/API calls and the exact audit log fields?

-Karthik
Network & Infra Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-19T11:02:00Z
Subject: RE: Private deployment cutover: EU->APAC node affinity and evacuation planning

Adding the concrete steps and audit field names below (draft):

API/CLI sequence (high level):
1) redwood tenant freeze --tenant acme-eu --mode read-only --reason "regulatory-hold"
2) redwood snapshot create --tenant acme-eu --manifest-id {{uuid}} --kms-metadata "region=eu;key-id=kms-eu-1"
3) redwood snapshot export --manifest-id {{uuid}} --dest s3://acme-evidence-eu/{{manifest}} --sign-with tenant-signature
4) redwood routing promote --tenant acme --from eu-cluster --to apac-cluster --auth-token {{signed-token}}
5) redwood audit append --event-type evacuation --manifest {{manifest}} --actor {{operator}} --hash {{sha256}}

Audit fields (required):
- event_id (uuid)
- tenant_id
- operator_id
- timestamp_utc
- action (freeze|snapshot|export|promote|revert)
- manifest_id
- kms_key_id
- signature_proof (base64)

I also added two low-risk defaults for Acme to accept:
- Default cross-border token TTL = 4 hours (configurable).
- Default cache TTL during promotion = 60 seconds.

I can convert this into a step-by-step playbook and produce example CLI output. Attaching the draft playbook link.

-Jordan
Sr. Product Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: John Li <john.li@acme-fin.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-20T15:45:00Z
Subject: RE: Private deployment cutover: EU->APAC node affinity and evacuation planning

John —

Thanks for the quick answers over email. Based on Acme's preference (regional KMS required) and your RPO target of ~2 minutes for warm standby, we recommend the following as acceptance criteria you can include in your cutover plan:

1) Data residency enforcement: routing tag + default EU-only routing. Cross-border tokens only on explicit signed approval.
2) KMS: customer-managed EU keys enforced. No key material exported; snapshots include KMS envelope metadata and remain stored in EU evidence buckets.
3) Evacuation playbook: follow the 5-step sequence Karthik/Jordan drafted (freeze -> snapshot -> export -> promote -> audit). We will provide CLI snippets and a signed manifest template.
4) Cache/TTL defaults: in-memory TTL 60s during promotion; persisted writes flushed to durable store before promote.

Next steps:
- If Acme accepts, we’ll produce a formal short playbook (2 pages) + example audit records and a sample manifest within 48 hours.
- Please confirm acceptance of the KMS constraint (EU-only) or flag if you need the transient-wrapping fallback.

If you confirm, we’ll schedule a 30-minute runbook review with your Cloud Ops team next week.

Best,
Evelyn
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: proposed-evacuation-playbook.md (final draft)]
